outcome: Incidence of suspected FGR (fetal growth retardation)
Incidence of miscarriages before 14 weeks of gestation
Incidence of miscarriages after 14 weeks of gestation
cohort: The study included 5137 mothers and newborns who presented at the University Hospital St. Hedwig, Regensburg, Germany, across pre-pandemic, pandemic lockdown, and post-pandemic periods.
finding: During the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown, there was a significantly lower incidence of hyperemesis gravidarum and suspected fetal growth retardation (FGR), with FGR incidence returning to pre-pandemic levels after restrictions were lifted.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome for all newborns.
gest_age: Measured as an outcome for all newborns, with specific analysis for preterm deliveries (<37 WG) and miscarriages (<14 WG and >=14 WG).
